title: English
description: ICSE Class X English: the ten prescribed Treasure Chest texts (five prose stories, five poems) relocated from the pre-reconciliation Class IX registry and published to the verified Appendix I placement; the Language paper is still to be verified.

syllabusBaselines.source: To be verified against the official board syllabus document.
syllabusBaselines.note: The overall Class X English Language and Literature syllabus is still unverified against an official source. Only the ten prescribed-text listings registered under the 2028 baseline below are published, and their chapter files carry no Language-paper content, so no unverified content is presented to students.

syllabusBaselines.source: CISCE ICSE Appendix I (Examination Year 2027 and 2028) as reproduced by Scribd and corroborated by Shaalaa, Oswal Publishers and Jagran Josh (cisce.org returned 403), consulted during the Class IX 2028 reconciliation.
syllabusBaselines.note: Scope: prescribed-text placement only. The same Appendix I reproductions that verify the Class IX Treasure Chest list place these ten titles under Class X — five prose stories (With the Photographer, The Elevator, The Girl Who Can, The Pedestrian, The Last Lesson) and five poems (Haunted Houses, The Glove and the Lions, When Great Trees Fall, A Considerable Speck, The Power of Music). On 2026-10-25, after the placement evidence was documented in the continuation ledger (Phase XIII), their chapter files were relocated intact from class-9/english and published here (10 chapters, 100 questions). The rest of the Class X English syllabus is not yet verified and has no chapter files.

sections.title: Literature in English
sections.description: Drama, prose and poetry: original summaries, analysis and practice. Read the prescribed text alongside these notes.

chapters.title: With the Photographer
chapters.author: Stephen Leacock
chapters.blurb: A comic visit to a portrait studio where the photographer rewrites the customer's face — Leacock's joke about experts, vanity and self-acceptance.

chapters.title: The Elevator
chapters.author: William Sleator
chapters.blurb: A boy's fear of a shuddering lift, an adult who refuses to listen, and a silent woman who knows his name.

chapters.title: The Girl Who Can
chapters.author: Ama Ata Aidoo
chapters.blurb: Adjoa's legs are judged at home and proven at school — a child's-eye story of gender expectation and a running trophy.

chapters.title: The Pedestrian
chapters.author: Ray Bradbury
chapters.blurb: A man who walks at night in a city that no longer walks, watches or reads.

chapters.title: The Last Lesson
chapters.author: Alphonse Daudet
chapters.blurb: A schoolboy's final French lesson in an Alsatian village under new rulers.

chapters.title: Haunted Houses
chapters.author: H. W. Longfellow
chapters.blurb: Why every house where people have lived is, in a sense, haunted.

chapters.title: The Glove and the Lions
chapters.author: Leigh Hunt
chapters.blurb: A lady's cruel test of love and a knight's answer, told at a royal lion fight.

chapters.title: When Great Trees Fall
chapters.author: Maya Angelou
chapters.blurb: How the loss of great people shakes the world, and how memory heals it.

chapters.title: A Considerable Speck
chapters.author: Robert Frost
chapters.blurb: A poet spares a tiny creature after recognising a mind at work in it.

chapters.title: The Power of Music
chapters.author: Sukumar Ray
chapters.blurb: Sukumar Ray's nonsense poem: a singer whose voice flattens the countryside until one sagacious billy goat answers back.
